correctness.rationale: In L(K_{p,q}), the selected edge ij has d(i)+d(j)−2 selected neighbors, so every nonempty component in the base graph is K_2 or a two-edge star. Counting labeled components gives the stated factorial weights: each pair of tips contributes 2!, component permutations contribute a!b!c!, and unused labels contribute u!v!. A star admits no further incident edge. Two covered endpoints on a new edge would yield two distinct selected neighbors of that new edge. If a singleton edge exists it can be extended using any unused vertex; if none exists, the only possible extension joins two unused vertices. This proves both polynomials and the EGF. The bounds s≤2p and 3s=2(p+q−u−v)−c give the maximum upper bounds; in the narrow range put h=2p−q≥1, so h has residues 0,2,1 when p+q has residues 0,1,2 respectively. The claimed maximizing b then equals h/3, (h−2)/3, (h−1)/3, with the corresponding a nonnegative since 2q−p≥p; the wide case uses p left-centered stars. The maximality branches give s=p+a or s=q+b, with the former even, and the specified star or matching constructions attain all stated minima. Comparing the extrema leaves just (2,2) and (3,4). For q≥2p, a full-coverage configuration with a singleton would force c=2p−q−3b≤0; if only the right side is required to be covered, equality forces q=2p and a=p. Thus c=u=0 for maximal sets and the stated wide polynomial, support and top coefficient follow.
residual_risks: Nonmaterial verification-count wording: the 735 arithmetic grid pairs include all 11 brute-force boards, so there are 724 distinct additional pairs, not 735. All 11, with 1,419,088 subsets, are correctly described as the brute-force set. The exact proof does not rely on the finite checks.

The later-dated Resultary rook record has an exactly equivalent maximal enumerator and wide spectrum; those portions are not distinct from it, and independent priority between the records is not claimed. value.rationale: Rook graphs are natural complete-factor Cartesian products. Counting all and especially inclusion-maximal packings distinguishes the size spectrum of locally unextendable configurations from the known-style maximum packing problem. The exact minimum and complete two-exception classification quantify when maximality forces optimality, while wide boards exhibit a full parity-restricted support, information not supplied by a maximum alone.
residual_risks: No complexity claim or extension to arbitrary line graphs; the novelty case is not that every individual packing component or maximal coefficient is distinct from later work.
